climate.overview_html: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center made this week's climate story explicit: the August ENSO Diagnostic Discussion puts the weekly Niño-3.4 index at +2.7°C on August 12 and assigns >90% probability that the 2026–27 event peaks at “super” strength (ONI comfortably above +2.0°C), with El Niño persisting near-certainly through the Atlantic hurricane season peak and into MAM 2027. The CPC seasonal outlook released August 20 shows a pronounced south-wet/north-warm winter split consistent with a strong El Niño teleconnection. Meanwhile Copernicus CAMS reports 2026 wildfire emissions between 60°–66.6°N running above the 2003–2025 mean and emissions above 66.6°N tracking among the highest Arctic-Circle years on record — Yamal-Nenets set its highest daily GFAS emission ever in August — with smoke transported around the Northern Hemisphere and across the Arctic Ocean as Indonesia's El Niño-primed fire season starts unusually hot in Kalimantan. Cryosphere signals continue to tilt negative: Arctic extent was 9th-lowest (NSIDC SII) on August 16, ESA Sentinel-1 imagery documents an ongoing ~76 km² tabular calving at Petermann (the largest Arctic calving since 2020), and — on the governance side — NOAA notified authors on August 11 that it will end administrative support for the 20-year Arctic Report Card, imperiling the December 2026 edition.

items.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center / The Hill
items.headline: NOAA CPC Fall/Winter Seasonal Outlook: >90% Probability of a ‘Super’ El Niño by Early Winter; South-Wet / North-Warm Winter Split Now Locked In
items.summary: NOAA CPC's September–November and December–February seasonal outlooks show most of the CONUS favored to run warmer than average through fall, with the Southwest and Southeast tilting wet and the Pacific Northwest and Northeast tilting dry. Forecasters put the probability that the 2026–27 El Niño reaches ‘super’ strength (ONI comfortably above +2.0°C) at greater than 90%, with maximum intensity expected late fall to early winter. The winter maps display the canonical strong-Niño pattern: stormy southern-tier subtropical jet, warm North, and drier-than-normal Pacific Northwest — consistent with the sharpest El Niño teleconnection signal in at least a decade. Downstream reporting in KLTV's local summary and Unofficial Networks' winter-map recap emphasized the outlook's implications for Southeast agriculture, California water supply, and northern-tier ski operators. NOAA's mid-August ENSO Diagnostic Discussion complements the outlook with the observation that no ENSO transition is likely before spring 2027 — El Niño will dominate the Northern Hemisphere winter.

items.source: NOAA CPC ENSO Discussion / Action News 5
items.headline: August ENSO Diagnostic Discussion: Weekly Niño-3.4 Hits +2.7°C on August 12; 100% Probability of El Niño Through Peak Atlantic Hurricane Season
items.summary: The August 2026 NOAA CPC ENSO Diagnostic Discussion places the weekly Niño-3.4 index at +2.7°C on 12 August 2026, up from a May–July seasonal mean of +1.51°C and a July monthly of +2.03°C. NOAA assigns greater than 90% probability to strong or very strong El Niño conditions during August–October 2026, and 100% probability of El Niño persisting through the Atlantic hurricane season peak (September). The mid-August objective outlook shows no indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027; the March–April–May 2027 forecast still favors moderate-to-strong El Niño, implying an unusually durable event. Downstream Action News 5 coverage on August 17 emphasized the persistence signal for U.S. winter temperature and precipitation patterns and the dominance of El Niño-driven upper-level wind shear as the mechanism suppressing this year's Atlantic hurricane season.

items.headline: CAMS: Arctic-Circle Wildfire Emissions Among Highest on Record; Yamal-Nenets Sets Daily GFAS Record; Smoke Crosses Arctic as Indonesia's El-Niño Fire Season Ignites
items.summary: The Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service reports that 2026 wildfire emissions between 60°–66.6°N are running above the 2003–2025 GFAS mean and that emissions north of 66.6°N make 2026 one of the highest Arctic-Circle years on record. Yamal-Nenets Autonomous Okrug set its highest daily total-emissions value in the GFAS record during August, with heavy concurrent burning in Krasnoyarsk Krai and the Sakha Republic; Canada's Northwest Territories and British Columbia remain highly active. Thick smoke from both North American and eastern Russian fires was transported around the Northern Hemisphere and across the Arctic Ocean, seeding aerosol-loading anomalies at high latitudes. Meanwhile Indonesia's seasonal fires — mainly in West and Central Kalimantan on Borneo — began unusually early and intense under the developing strong El Niño, with cross-border air-quality impacts reaching Singapore and Malaysia. CAMS frames the pattern as an increasingly synchronized boreal-plus-Maritime-Continent fire regime under strong-Niño teleconnections.

items.headline: Mercator MHW Bulletin (22 Aug): Southern Ocean 45°–60°S MHW Persists; Mediterranean Intensifies South of Sicily as North Atlantic Cools
items.summary: The Mercator Ocean International marine heatwave bulletin for 22 August finds a large Southern Ocean MHW between 50°E–80°E, 45°S–60°S stable in area and holding moderate-to-strong intensity. The Mediterranean MHW is contracting in areal extent but intensifying south of Sicily, where nearly all pixels are now classified ‘strong’; heatwaves off southern France, near Gibraltar, and from southern Greece eastward have essentially dissipated. In the North Atlantic, the MHW is shrinking in both area and intensity, with only pockets north of Spain, around the Canaries, and near 30°N central-basin still classified ‘strong,’ the rest downgraded to moderate. Context: July 2026 posted MHW coverage over 37% of the global ocean — the second-highest for any month in the 1991–present record — so the mid-August contraction should be read as a modest normalization from an extreme baseline rather than a return to climatology.

items.source: Alaska and Arctic Climate (Rick Thoman) / UK Met Office
items.headline: Arctic Sea Ice August Update: 8th-Lowest (JAXA) / 9th-Lowest (NSIDC) on Aug 16; Chukchi and Beaufort Melt Accelerates After Early-Month Pause
items.summary: Rick Thoman's mid-August update reports Arctic-wide sea-ice extent on 16 August ranked 8th-lowest (JAXA) / 9th-lowest (NSIDC Sea Ice Index) in the satellite record. The daily-melt trajectory resembled recent years with the notable exception of an unusual late-July-to-early-August slow-down. In the first half of August, large stretches of open water opened north and northwest of Alaska in the Chukchi and Beaufort seas, and conditions in the Laptev, Kara, Barents seas and east Greenland account for most of the total deficit. The annual minimum is roughly four weeks out. A companion Met Office briefing recorded 7.02 million km² on 2 August (1.38 million km² below the 1981–2010 mean) and Antarctic extent at 16.65 million km² — the 4th-lowest for the date. Combined with the persistent strong El Niño signal and record boreal fire emissions, the Arctic remains this season's most stressed regional Earth-system indicator.

items.headline: China Briefing: 15th Five-Year Plan for Coal Pledges Peaking ‘During the Plan Period’ but Sets No Firm Year; Ecology Plan Targets 25.8% Forest Cover by 2030
items.summary: Carbon Brief's biweekly China Briefing analyzes the newly released 15th Five-Year Plan for coal (2026–2030), released 10 August by the National Development and Reform Commission and the National Energy Administration. The plan pledges peaking coal use during the plan period but does not set a specific peaking year or a hard production cap, and requires all new capacity to be centrally approved via a ‘single ledger’ mechanism. Kevin Tu of Columbia's Center on Global Energy Policy calls it ‘neither a coal phase-out nor phase-down plan’ and says it gives Beijing ‘considerable flexibility.’ In parallel, China released a 15th Five-Year Plan for ecological protection aiming to raise forest cover to 25.8% by 2030, and Qiushi republished excerpts of an April Xi Jinping speech on natural-disaster prevention. The People's Bank of China's 2026–30 ‘reform and development plan’ adds a quality/effectiveness target for low-carbon finance.

items.headline: NOAA to End Administrative Support for the Arctic Report Card After 20 Years; December 2026 Edition Searching for a Non-Federal Host
items.summary: NOAA notified Arctic Report Card authors on 11 August that it would end administrative support for the 20-year-old peer-reviewed annual assessment. The op-ed argues the report's integrated tracking of sea ice, glaciers, permafrost, boreal forests and coastal Alaska communities is uniquely difficult to reconstitute outside NOAA because the agency provided coordination, production, technical, and media resources on top of the underlying science. Work on the 2026 edition — due December — is already underway; lead editors are searching for a non-NOAA host. Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) publicly criticized the decision. The move lands at a moment when the Arctic Report Card's audience — Alaskan communities, U.S. defense and shipping stakeholders, and the international cryosphere community — has arguably never needed synthesis more.

items.headline: Sentinel-1 Documents Ongoing Petermann Ice-Tongue Disintegration: ~76 km² Tabular Berg Calved Aug 4; Two More Rifts (~97 km² and ~87 km²) Under Watch
items.summary: ESA's Sentinel-1 SAR imagery documents the 4 August calving of a ~76 km² tabular iceberg (~150 m thick, roughly Manhattan-sized) from the Petermann Glacier ice tongue in northwest Greenland — the glacier's largest floating-ice loss since 2012 and the largest Arctic calving event since 2020. Sentinel-1's C-band radar can image through polar night and cloud cover, making it uniquely suited to tracking the evolving rift network on the Petermann tongue. ESA highlights two further rifts that could shed slabs of approximately 97 km² and 87 km² as the tongue continues to disintegrate. Petermann is the largest floating glacier in Greenland and one of only three that still maintain a semi-permanent ice shelf; its ongoing structural retreat is one of the clearest visual indicators of the ocean-side heat forcing driving ice-sheet mass loss.

items.headline: Bloomberg: Rhine at ~15 cm at Kaub on Aug 11; Danube-Cooled Nuclear Throttled; Europe's Heat-Death Toll Passes 25,000 as Maize and Sunflower Yields Drop 6–7%
items.summary: Bloomberg quantifies the cascading July–August heat damage across the European economy. The Rhine at Germany's Kaub gauge fell to a navigable depth near 15 cm on 11 August (records begin in 1880), forcing barges to run at fractional loads. Hungarian and Romanian nuclear stations cooled by the Danube throttled back generation because of inlet temperatures. Continent-wide heat-related mortality passed 25,000 through July, with Germany's Robert Koch Institute putting the German figure at 11,900 and France reporting more than 5,700 through 2 July. Maize and sunflower yields are down 6–7% versus prior estimates. Bloomberg puts the seasonal economic bill in the hundreds of billions of euros. A companion 11 August piece on Rhine industry impacts details barge-load penalties and chemical-plant feedstock disruption at BASF's Ludwigshafen complex.

major_events.name: Typhoon Saudel (WP17 / Philippine name Obet) — Near-Super Typhoon; PAR Entry Aug 24; Okinawa/Amami Direct Approach ~06 UTC Aug 26
major_events.status: NEAR-SUPER TYPHOON · ~95 KT · ~944 HPA · SUPER-TYPHOON POTENTIAL BEFORE PEAK
major_events.impact: As of 00 UTC 24 August, JMA analyzed Saudel at ~944 hPa with 10-min max winds ~110 kt near 23.9°N, 136.3°E, moving WNW at ~30 km/h. PAGASA classifies it as near-super typhoon strength (~175 km/h sustained, gusts to 215 km/h) and says Saudel will enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility Monday afternoon (24 Aug) as ‘Obet’; further intensification to super-typhoon status remains on the table. No Philippine landfall is expected but Saudel will substantially enhance the southwest monsoon (habagat) over western Luzon through the week. JMA and JTWC put closest approach to Okinawa's main island and Amami Oshima around 06 UTC 26 Aug with violent winds (JTWC ~104 mph), torrential rainfall, and dangerous storm surge. Post-Ryukyu track guidance is diverging — KMA increasingly signals downstream risk to the Korean Peninsula while JMA tracks the center south of Japan's main islands and some ECMWF members target eastern China.

major_events.name: US South Heat Dome — REBUILDING (Correction from Yesterday); 30M+ Under ‘Extreme’ Heat Aug 24–29
major_events.status: RE-INTENSIFYING · HEAT INDEX 105–115°F FORECAST FROM TEXAS TO CAROLINAS
major_events.impact: The 21-day Gulf-South heat dome that dominated early-to-mid August is not abating as forecast on August 23 — it is rebuilding for a second act. Weather.com and AccuWeather forecast dozens of daily-high-temperature and monthly high-pressure records under threat this week, with widespread ~100°F highs from Oklahoma/Texas east to the Carolinas and mid-90s in Florida. NOAA has more than 30 million Americans under ‘extreme’ heat risk and roughly 50 million under ‘major’ heat risk. Elevated overnight lows across the Southeast raise heat-illness risk further. The pattern is expected to persist through the weekend.

major_events.name: British Columbia Wildfire State of Emergency — 100+ Active Fires; Bald Range Fire ~9,500 ha; Cross-Border Smoke to Northern-Tier US
major_events.status: PROVINCIAL STATE OF EMERGENCY · WIDESPREAD EVACUATIONS · SMOKE PLUME OVER US
major_events.impact: British Columbia is under a provincial state of emergency declared by Premier David Eby earlier in August with more than 100 active wildfires burning. The Bald Range fire has grown to approximately 9,500 ha with evacuation orders across Summerland, Peachland, and neighboring west Okanagan communities. Persistent heat and precipitation deficit through July–August continue to drive intense fire activity in the Fraser Canyon and Okanagan Valley. Smoke plumes are again transported south into Washington, Idaho, Montana, and the Dakotas; air-quality alerts are expected across the northern-tier US through the coming week.

major_events.name: Europe Very-Extreme Fire Danger + Balkans Heat Dome — Romania/Hungary Corridor Through Aug 26
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS's fire-danger forecast shows very-extreme conditions dominating a large zone centered on Romania and Hungary through August 26, extending into the broader Balkans, Ukraine, and western Russia. Extreme danger conditions reach southern Ireland and central-southern Italy. A fresh heat-dome ridge is targeting Central Europe and the Balkans with 40°C-plus highs and elevated fire weather for the second half of the week. The Danube's record-low flow is stressing river-cooled thermal generation in Hungary and Romania; the Greece Attica multi-front fire complex (Porto Germeno, Salamis Island) is largely contained but Meltemi winds keep crews on alert.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — 2026 Toll ≥126; New Heavy-Rain Pulse in Progress
major_events.status: ONGOING · FLASH FLOODING ACROSS PUNJAB / KP / SINDH
major_events.impact: Cumulative deaths from rain-related incidents since 26 June have passed 126 per PDMA/Arab News reporting. A new heavy-rain pulse is producing flash flooding and urban flooding across northern and central Pakistan, with PMD flagging further heavy-rain risk over the next several days. The 2026 monsoon is running hot with successive flash-flood pulses across Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Sindh. Not on the 2022 catastrophic scale, but on pace to be one of the more damaging monsoons of the decade.

major_events.name: Atlantic Basin — Quiet But Watching Invests 97L and 98L; Below-Normal Season Signal Holding
major_events.status: QUIET · NO ACTIVE NAMED STORMS · 10% NHC 48-H FORMATION ODDS
major_events.impact: The Atlantic basin remains quiet as of August 24 with no active named storms. NHC's 48-hour formation odds are ~10%, focused on a non-tropical low west of Portugal that may briefly acquire subtropical characteristics. Invest 97L (central Atlantic near 25°N/50°W) and 98L (eastern Atlantic near 30°W) are tracking west; 97L development is considered highly likely by week's end but on a recurving track away from the US, while 98L is ingesting dry air. Consistent with NOAA's August 75%-below-normal-season outlook and continued El Niño wind-shear suppression. The MDR wave train suggests early September could break the lull.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Iselle (East Pacific) — 45 kt Fish Storm; No Land Threat
major_events.status: TROPICAL STORM · 45 KT · NW AT 10 KT · OPEN OCEAN
major_events.impact: As of 03 UTC 24 August, Iselle is at 17.1°N, 115.3°W with max sustained winds ~45 kt, gusts ~55 kt, moving NW at 10 kt. NHC has begun issuing full advisories. Iselle may briefly touch hurricane strength in the next ~36 hours before shear, cooler SSTs, and drier air erode it. Track keeps it well away from Mexico and Hawaii — an open-ocean fish storm. Marine advisories are out for Revillagigedo waters where an adjacent broad low (invests EP91/EP92) is producing gale-force winds.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Saudel reached near-super typhoon intensity (~95 kt / ~944 hPa) by 00 UTC on August 24 and is on the doorstep of the Philippine Area of Responsibility, expected to enter PAR Monday afternoon as Obet. No Philippine landfall is projected but a violent-typhoon-strength direct approach to Okinawa and Amami Oshima is still tracked for ~06 UTC August 26 with downstream KMA runs increasingly flagging Korean-peninsula risk. In the US, yesterday's read that the Southern heat dome was abating is superseded — the pattern re-intensified over the weekend and is now expected to break dozens of daily records with 30 million-plus under ‘extreme’ heat risk through August 29. British Columbia is under a provincial state of emergency with 100+ active fires including the ~9,500 ha Bald Range fire, and smoke is again pouring south into the northern-tier US. The Romania–Hungary very-extreme fire danger corridor persists through August 26 as a fresh Balkans heat dome pushes 40°C+ highs; Pakistan's monsoon death toll has passed 126 with a new heavy-rain pulse in progress; the Atlantic remains quiet despite invests 97L/98L; and Tropical Storm Iselle spins as an open-ocean fish storm in the East Pacific.

items.headline: Saudel Reaches Near-Super Typhoon Strength — 95 kt / 944 hPa; PAR Entry Monday PM as ‘Obet’; Okinawa/Amami Direct Approach Aug 26; Korea Signal Strengthens Post-Ryukyu
items.summary: Typhoon Saudel (WP17) reached near-super typhoon intensity by 00 UTC 24 August 2026: JMA analysis ~944 hPa with 10-minute maximum sustained winds around 110 kt and JMA forecast peak pressure ~925 hPa with 180 km/h 10-min winds by 06 UTC 24 August. PAGASA reports gusts to 215 km/h and 175 km/h sustained. Saudel is centered near 23.9°N, 136.3°E and moving WNW at ~30 km/h. It is expected to enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility Monday afternoon (24 Aug) and receive the local name ‘Obet.’ PAGASA warns further intensification to super-typhoon status cannot be ruled out before or after PAR entry. No Philippine landfall is expected, but Saudel will substantially enhance the southwest monsoon (habagat) and drench western Luzon with heavy rains through the week. Marine warning area is expanding from 70 NM (21 Aug) to 270 NM by 25 Aug. JMA and JTWC both track closest approach to Okinawa's main island and Amami Oshima around 06 UTC 26 Aug with violent winds (JTWC ~104 mph), torrential rainfall, and dangerous coastal inundation. Post-Ryukyu track guidance is diverging: KMA increasingly signals downstream risk to the Korean Peninsula while JMA carries the center south of Japan's main islands and some ECMWF members target eastern China.

items.headline: US South Heat Dome Rebuilds — Dozens of Daily Records Under Threat Aug 24–29; 30M Under ‘Extreme’ Heat, 50M Under ‘Major’
items.summary: Weather.com's August 23 regional forecast documents a re-intensifying heat dome across the U.S. Deep South and Southeast through August 29 — reversing the mid-week assumption that the pattern was breaking down. Widespread ~100°F highs are forecast from Oklahoma and Texas east to the Carolinas, with mid-90s in Florida and heat indices of 105–115°F. AccuWeather flags dozens of daily-high-temperature and monthly high-pressure records under threat. Elevated overnight lows across the Southeast raise heat-illness risk further and stress agricultural and electricity systems already tested by earlier August. NOAA has more than 30 million Americans under ‘extreme’ heat risk and roughly 50 million under ‘major’ heat risk. The Hill notes that this second wave arrives as El Niño-driven upper-level ridging over the subtropical Atlantic reinforces the pattern; frontal-boundary progression across the Deep South is now delayed until at least the weekend.

items.source: Government of Canada / Al Jazeera / Washington Post
items.headline: British Columbia Under Provincial State of Emergency: 100+ Active Fires; ~9,500 ha Bald Range Fire Evacuations; Smoke Plume Again Crossing Into US
items.summary: The Government of Canada's August update reports that British Columbia remains under a provincial state of emergency declared by Premier David Eby earlier in August with more than 100 active wildfires. The Bald Range fire has grown to approximately 9,500 hectares with evacuation orders across Summerland, Peachland, and neighboring west Okanagan communities. Southern BC's persistent heat and precipitation deficit through July–August continue to drive intense fire activity in the Fraser Canyon and Okanagan Valley. Cross-border smoke transport is again a headline U.S. story: fresh weekend fire growth has pushed thick plumes south into Washington, Idaho, Montana, and the Dakotas, with air-quality alerts likely for northwestern and north-central U.S. states through the coming week. The Washington Post separately reports smoke ‘once again pouring across the U.S.’ The season-to-date pattern reinforces the CAMS finding that boreal wildfire emissions between 60°–66.6°N are running above the 2003–2025 mean.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Iselle Named in Eastern Pacific — 45 kt Fish Storm; May Briefly Reach Hurricane Strength Before Shear Kills It; No Land Threat
items.summary: The NHC named Tropical Storm Iselle in the eastern Pacific on August 23. As of 03 UTC 24 August, Iselle was near 17.1°N, 115.3°W with max sustained winds ~45 kt (~52 mph), gusts ~55 kt, moving NW at ~10 kt. Iselle is expected to strengthen and may briefly touch minimal hurricane strength in the next ~36 hours before more hostile shear, cooler SSTs, and drier air erode it. The track keeps Iselle well away from Mexico and Hawaii — an open-ocean fish storm with no land impacts expected. Marine advisories are out for Revillagigedo waters where an adjacent broad low (invests EP91/EP92) is producing gale-force winds. Dr. Ryan Maue's Weather Substack tropics roundup for 23 August also notes the East Pacific-in-summer signal has returned to near-normal after early-season quiet.

items.headline: Europe Heat Dome Shifts East to Central Europe / Balkans — 40°C-Plus Highs and Very-Extreme Fire Danger Persist Through Aug 26
items.summary: The persistent European heat-dome pattern that produced the continent's warmest June–July on record has re-shifted east with a fresh ridge targeting Central Europe and the Balkans, delivering 40°C-plus highs and elevated fire-weather conditions through August 26. JRC EFFIS's fire-danger forecast keeps very-extreme conditions dominating a Romania–Hungary corridor, extending into the broader Balkans, Ukraine, and western Russia; extreme danger conditions also reach southern Ireland and central-southern Italy. Hundreds of scattered fires are burning in Romania; the Danube's record-low flow is stressing river-cooled thermal generation in Hungary and Romania. Greece's Attica multi-front fire complex is largely contained but Meltemi winds and 40°C temperatures forecast late-week could spike fire risk again. NPR's parallel reporting frames the pattern as a compound heat–drought–energy crisis rather than a single-hazard event.

items.source: Arab News / PMD / NASA Earth Observatory
items.headline: Pakistan Monsoon Toll Passes 126 Since June 26; New Heavy-Rain Pulse Producing Flash Flooding Across Punjab, KP, Sindh
items.summary: Arab News reports Pakistan's cumulative death toll from rain-related incidents since 26 June has passed 126, citing PDMA figures. A new heavy-rain pulse is producing flash flooding and urban flooding across northern and central Pakistan, with PMD flagging further heavy-rain risk over the next several days. The 2026 monsoon has been running hot with successive flash-flood pulses across Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Sindh; NASA Earth Observatory imagery documents extensive floodplain inundation across the Indus system. The event is not on the 2022 catastrophic scale, but on pace to be one of the more damaging monsoons of the decade. Regional context: the developing strong El Niño and concurrent positive Indian Ocean Dipole historically increase monsoon-season pluvial extremes in the northern subcontinent while depressing rainfall in eastern Africa and Australia.

renewables.overview_html: This week's renewables headlines paired a milestone-scale hybrid solar-plus-storage bring-online with a milestone-scale hybrid PPA on opposite ends of the development cycle. Scatec brought the second and final phase of its 1,125 MW Obelisk hybrid in Aswan, Egypt, to commercial operations — Africa's largest solar-plus-storage installation (1,125 MW PV + 100 MW/200 MWh BESS) contracted under a 25-year USD PPA with EETC. In the U.S., EDF Power Solutions signed two 25-year PPAs with NV Energy for the 400 MWac / 400 MW / 1,600 MWh (4-hour) Winston Energy Project in Lyon County, Nevada — one of the summer's largest U.S. IOU solar-plus-storage PPAs. Global PV crossed a symbolic threshold as BloombergNEF flagged 3 TW installed — the third terawatt added in under two years. Grid and storage: Bulgaria's operating BESS fleet jumped from 4.4 GW to 5.4 GW in a month as Recovery Plan deadlines forced a wave of commissioning tests, and the UK granted DCO for the 400 MW / 600 MVA Beacon Fen solar+BESS park. Offshore wind: ScottishPower Renewables and Masdar completed the last of 95 monopile foundations at the 1.4 GW East Anglia THREE project in the UK North Sea.

items.headline: Scatec Brings Final Phase of 1.1 GW Obelisk Hybrid Online — Africa's Largest Solar-Plus-Storage; 25-Year USD PPA with EETC; ~3 TWh/yr, ~1.2 Mt CO₂/yr Displaced
items.summary: Scatec reached commercial operations on the second and final phase of its Obelisk project in Aswan, Egypt, taking the plant to 1,125 MW of PV coupled with a 100 MW / 200 MWh Li-ion BESS — the largest hybrid solar-plus-storage installation in Africa. Phase 1 delivered 561 MW of PV alongside the full storage system; Phase 2 adds a further 564 MW of PV. Output is contracted under a 25-year USD-denominated power purchase agreement with the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company (EETC) signed in November 2024. The plant is expected to deliver roughly 3,000 GWh per year and displace about 1.2 Mt CO₂ per year. Notable for meteorologists and system operators: the paired storage is sized only for evening-peak arbitrage, not intraday load-following — a template that appears likely to spread across MENA irradiance markets as auction-price competition prioritizes the cheapest possible dispatch shape.

items.headline: EDF Power Solutions Signs 25-Year NV Energy PPAs for ‘Winston’ Project: 400 MWac Solar + 400 MW/1,600 MWh BESS in Lyon County, Nevada; Online 2029
items.summary: EDF Power Solutions North America executed two 25-year power purchase agreements with NV Energy for the Winston Energy Project, a 400 MWac PV plant co-located with a 400 MW / 1,600 MWh (4-hour) battery energy storage system in Lyon County, Nevada. First delivery is targeted for October 2029. Expected annual production is approximately 1.11 TWh — enough to serve about 100,000 homes — with roughly USD 100 million in local tax revenue over the project's life. The Winston PPA is among the largest U.S. IOU-signed solar-plus-storage contracts of the summer and reinforces the 4-hour BESS duration standardization that is emerging as the Desert Southwest default. NV Energy's deep summer peaks and El Niño-linked shift in Great Basin storminess make paired storage particularly valuable for reserve margins.

items.headline: Global Installed PV Crosses 3 TW — Third Terawatt Added in Under Two Years; BNEF Projects >9 TW by 2036
items.summary: Global installed photovoltaic capacity crossed 3 TW this month according to BloombergNEF. The third terawatt was added in under two years, versus roughly a decade for the first (100 GW → 1 TW). China remains the dominant driver of new adds, though emerging markets (India, Brazil, MENA) contributed a growing share of the incremental terawatt. BNEF projects greater than 9 TW installed globally by 2036 under its central scenario. The threshold is a useful framing indicator for medium-term generation-mix, curtailment, and duck-curve forecasting; combined with 2026's record-low module prices and the sharp acceleration in AI data-center corporate PPAs, it suggests solar's structural share of new-generation adds will continue outpacing prior IEA / BNEF projections through the second half of the decade.

items.headline: East Anglia THREE Passes Foundation Milestone — All 95 Monopiles and Transition Pieces Installed at 1.4 GW UK Offshore Project; SPR/Masdar Target End-2026 COD
items.summary: Seaway7 finished installation of all 95 monopile foundations (1,200–1,800 tonnes, 67–84 m tall — the largest ever set from a jack-up vessel in Europe) and 95 transition pieces at the GBP 4 billion, 1.4 GW East Anglia THREE offshore wind project in the UK North Sea. Turbine installation is already underway; ScottishPower Renewables and joint-venture partner Masdar continue to target full commercial operation by end-2026. The project uses Siemens Gamesa 14 MW-class turbines and is a key contributor to the UK's near-term 50 GW-by-2030 offshore wind ambition. The foundation-scale milestone signals that European heavy-lift and monopile-manufacturing bottlenecks flagged in 2024–2025 have eased at least at the tier-one supplier level.

items.headline: Bulgaria's Operating BESS Fleet Jumps From 4.4 GW to 5.4 GW in a Month — Rush of Recovery-Plan Commissioning; Batteries Now 22.8% of Installed Capacity
items.summary: ENTSO-E data as of 17 August 2026 shows Bulgarian operating battery-storage capacity up approximately 23% month-on-month, from 4.4 GW on 10 July to 5.4 GW — driven by a rush of commissioning ahead of the country's Recovery Plan and RESTORE grant deadlines (build by 31 July 2026 and full charge–discharge cycle tests by end-August). Batteries now make up ~22.8% of Bulgaria's 23.75 GW installed capacity, and roughly 69% of the combined solar-plus-wind base — putting the country well ahead of its 2030 policy targets on paper. The dataset is a notable ancillary-services and imbalance-price signal for the SEE market and offers a natural experiment in what happens to system balancing and price formation when battery penetration doubles in a single year.

items.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
items.headline: UK Grants DCO for 400 MW Beacon Fen Solar + 600 MVA BESS (Lincolnshire) Over County Council Objection
items.summary: The UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) approved the Development Consent Order for Low Carbon's Beacon Fen Energy Park east of Sleaford, Lincolnshire. The project comprises up to 400 MW of PV, up to 600 MVA of battery storage, an on-site substation, and a 400 kV grid connection into the Bicker Fen substation. The examination began in April 2025 and the Planning Inspectorate submitted its recommendation in May 2026; consent was granted despite Lincolnshire County Council opposition on landscape and agricultural-land grounds. Beacon Fen adds to the UK's growing NSIP-scale solar pipeline as it works toward the 70 GW-by-2035 solar target set out in the 2024 Clean Power Action Plan. The DCO precedent — consent granted over county-council objection on prime-farmland grounds — is watched closely by other Fen-belt developers.

science.overview_html: The week's headline research thread is a hard-eyed audit of AI weather and climate models. A Köppen-Geiger climate-zone decomposition of the AIMIP Phase 1 model suite under prescribed +4K SST forcing (Merchant, Klöwer, Christensen and co-authors) finds that only the hybrid NeuralGCM-HRD reorganizes climate zones in a way consistent with known thermodynamic and hydrological scaling — a benchmark result for whether emulator-style AI climate models have learned generalizable physics or just present-day statistics. On the forecasting side, Tianmu-TC proposes a physics-constrained conditional diffusion framework that claims to beat ECMWF on TC track and intensity across multiple basins at substantially lower compute, and BaguanHR attacks the data bottleneck for 0.1° global ML forecasting by super-resolving ERA5 into a synthetic training corpus. Beyond AI, the LMR4D-Var paleoclimate framework deploys full 4D-Var against multi-timescale proxies for the first time, and a Nature Climate Change paper quantifies how PM2.5 aerosol asymmetrically depresses plant water-use efficiency — a feedback most Earth-system models still miss.

items.headline: AI Climate Models Reproduce Present-Day Climate but Struggle With +4K Zone Reorganization — Only Hybrid NeuralGCM-HRD Reorganizes Köppen-Geiger Zones Consistently
items.meta: Merchant, Klöwer, Stanley-Clamp, Höver, Michel, Groot, Christensen · arXiv:2608.17986 · physics.ao-ph
items.summary: This paper applies a Köppen-Geiger climate-zone decomposition to the AIMIP Phase 1 suite of AI climate models under prescribed +4K SST forcing and compares responses to physics-based AMIP models. All AI models reproduce the 1979–2014 ERA5 baseline climatology within the physics-based spread for temperature, precipitation, and near-surface humidity. However, under +4K only the hybrid NeuralGCM-HRD reorganizes climate zones in a way consistent with established thermodynamic and hydrological scaling relations; other AI models show physically inconsistent zone reorganizations that would produce misleading downscaling and risk projections. The paper is a direct benchmark for whether emulator-style AI climate models have learned generalizable physics or just memorized present-day statistics — an urgent question for anyone using AI models for climate risk, hydrological impact, or renewable-siting analysis out of sample.

items.headline: Tianmu-TC: Physics-Constrained Conditional Diffusion Beats ECMWF on Global TC Track and Intensity at Lower Compute
items.meta: Shiqi Zhang et al. · arXiv:2608.18500 · physics.ao-ph
items.summary: Tianmu-TC recasts tropical cyclone track and intensity forecasting as a controllable generative process using a physics-constrained conditional diffusion framework trained on Western North Pacific data. The authors report that Tianmu-TC outperforms deterministic and ensemble AI baselines and authoritative NWP systems including ECMWF across multiple global ocean basins, at substantially lower computational cost. The physics constraints target dynamical balance conditions rather than direct pixel-space regularization, an approach that has become increasingly popular in atmospheric generative modeling. The paper adds to a busy 2026 season of purpose-built TC-AI systems and offers a probabilistic alternative to correction-style approaches like AIFS-TC. Operational implications: TC forecasting is now unambiguously a domain where physics-informed generative ML competes with — and in some scenarios beats — the world's flagship NWP systems.

items.headline: BaguanHR: Pushing ML Global Weather Forecasting to 0.1° via a Provably-Cheaper Data-Transfer Framework
items.meta: Yang Zhao, Peisong Niu, Tian Zhou, Ziqing Ma, Guanlong Ma, Rong Jin, Huiling Yuan, Liang Sun · arXiv:2608.14652
items.summary: BaguanHR argues that the bottleneck for 0.1° global ML weather models is data availability (ERA5 only exists at 0.25°), not architecture. The framework recasts the problem as data transfer: a variable-wise super-resolution step — whose conditional entropy is provably lower than end-to-end forecasting — is used to synthesize a 0.1° training corpus from ERA5, on top of which a global forecaster is trained on synthetic-plus-real data. The authors report beating both ML baselines and IFS-HRES on more than 85% of metrics on their evaluation suite. The result matters for renewable-energy and TC applications where mesoscale features (frontal structure, land-sea breeze, coastline convergence) sit at or below the 0.25° grid — and where the historic ML NWP alternative was to run high-resolution NWP just to generate the training data.

items.headline: LMR4D-Var: Coupled Multiscale Paleoclimate Reconstruction Using Full 4D Variational Assimilation Beats Ensemble-Kalman Predecessors on Instrumental Verification
items.meta: Zilu Meng, Gregory J. Hakim, Julien Emile-Geay, Tanaya Gondhalekar, Eric J. Steig · arXiv:2608.19469 · physics.ao-ph
items.summary: The Last Millennium Reanalysis 4D-Var (LMR4D-Var) framework reconstructs coupled climate trajectories from PAGES2k proxies, Temp12k, and borehole temperature profiles by jointly balancing model, observation, and initial-condition errors — a rare deployment of full 4D variational assimilation against heterogeneous multi-timescale proxy data rather than the ensemble Kalman flavor that has dominated paleoclimate reanalysis work. Instrumental verification (post-1850) shows LMR4D-Var produces the highest skill among available LMR reconstructions across the last millennium. The framework opens the door to consistent uncertainty-quantified reconstructions of coupled ocean-atmosphere states over the pre-instrumental period, which has direct implications for constraining natural-variability envelopes in near-term climate projections.

items.headline: ECMWF Coupled Seasonal Forecast System — Counterfactual Sensitivity to CO₂ and Anthropogenic Aerosol Forcings
items.meta: Michael Mayer, Daniel J. Befort, Jacob Maddison, Antje Weisheimer · arXiv:2608.18712 · physics.ao-ph
items.summary: This ECMWF-authored study runs counterfactual seasonal hindcasts using the ECMWF coupled seasonal forecasting system under alternative CO₂ and anthropogenic-aerosol forcing scenarios, documenting the experimental design and the impact on modeled climate trends underlying seasonal predictions. Directly relevant to seasonal-to-decadal (S2D) forecasters and to renewable-energy operators using seasonal outlooks whose backdrop trends depend sensitively on aerosol assumptions — a systematic sensitivity was previously unquantified in ECMWF's operational system. The paper positions ECMWF's seasonal system for the coming CMIP7-era forcing conventions and provides a template other seasonal centers can follow to isolate aerosol-driven biases from ENSO-driven seasonal signals.

items.headline: Wind Farms as Sensor Arrays for Turbulent Atmospheric Boundary Layer Reconstruction
items.meta: Manuel Ayala, Dennice Gayme, Charles Meneveau · arXiv:2608.20582 · physics.flu-dyn / physics.ao-ph
items.summary: This Johns Hopkins-led paper proposes using the operational turbines of a wind farm as a spatially distributed sensor array to reconstruct the spatio-temporal structure of turbulent boundary-layer inflow. The framework combines SCADA-style turbine measurements with atmospheric-boundary-layer statistical structure to infer flow features at spatial scales that no fixed anemometer network could resolve at reasonable cost. Concretely useful for offshore-wind operators seeking cheap in-situ ABL diagnostics that also drive wake models and short-term power forecasts, and for wind-resource campaigns that increasingly rely on power-curve inversion rather than direct met-mast measurement. The approach echoes the WindBorne-style philosophy that the observation network itself is now the highest-leverage frontier of forecast-skill improvement.

items.headline: AIFS-TC: LLM-Designed TC Intensity Correction to ECMWF's AIFS Matches Operational Skill in Hours of Development
items.summary: AIFS-TC presents a simple post-processing correction to ECMWF's AIFS forecast for tropical cyclone intensity that is competitive with operational TC-intensity guidance. The remarkable methodological detail is that the correction system was autonomously designed by a large language model in a few hours, framing the paper as much a demonstration of LLM-driven scientific ML tooling as of TC forecasting per se. Together with Tianmu-TC (arXiv:2608.18500), the paper reinforces the emerging picture that hurricane-intensity forecasting — long the hardest problem in operational NWP — is now the domain where ML techniques deliver the largest and most reliable skill gains, whether by dedicated diffusion models or by lightweight LLM-generated correction pipelines.

items.headline: Gyuleva, Knutti, Noyelle et al.: Statistical Noise and Missing Forcings Limit Estimates of Earth's Feedback From Pattern-Effect Studies
items.meta: Gyuleva, Knutti, Noyelle et al. · arXiv:2608.13219 · physics.ao-ph
items.summary: This paper argues that widely cited historical ‘pattern-effect’ estimates of Earth's radiative feedback — derived from prescribed-SST atmosphere-only runs — are dominated by statistical noise and missing forcing terms rather than a robust physical signal. The authors show that plausible alternative forcing choices flip the sign of the estimated pattern-effect contribution to climate sensitivity in several published analyses. The implication is that reported constraints on equilibrium climate sensitivity derived from the pattern-effect literature are more uncertain than commonly reported and should not be treated as a strong prior when assessing near-term risk. A methodological warning shot for the pattern-effect discourse that is likely to be widely cited in the next generation of feedback-constraint papers.

items.headline: PM2.5 Depresses Plant Water-Use Efficiency Asymmetrically — Photosynthesis Suffers More Than Evapotranspiration; Aerosol–Canopy Chemistry Missing From Most ESMs
items.meta: Jian Wang, Yuyu Zhou, Chaoyang Wu · Nature Climate Change · August 2026
items.summary: Wang, Zhou, and Wu quantify how fine particulate pollution (PM2.5) affects vegetation water-use efficiency across ecosystem scales, finding an asymmetric response: PM2.5 depresses photosynthesis more strongly than it suppresses evapotranspiration, netting a mostly negative WUE effect. The result matters for coupled climate–vegetation feedbacks in Earth system models — most of which ignore aerosol–canopy chemistry — and for agriculture-facing renewable and climate-risk analytics, where declining WUE is a compounding stressor on regional water balance. The paper adds a mechanism-specific line item to the broader research showing that non-CO₂ atmospheric composition changes affect the terrestrial carbon and water cycles in ways that are systematically excluded from current-generation climate projections.

items.headline: Holm: The Geometry of Stochastic Fluid Dynamics — Pedagogical Review of SALT / LA-SALT for Uncertainty Quantification in Ocean-Atmosphere Modeling
items.summary: Darryl Holm's pedagogical review lays out the geometric-mechanics foundations behind Stochastic Advection by Lie Transport (SALT) and its Location-Averaged (LA-SALT) variant — the increasingly popular family of structure-preserving stochastic parameterizations for uncertainty quantification in fluid dynamics. The review is aimed at researchers who want a clear derivation of why the SALT approach preserves conservation laws and momentum-map structure while adding physically motivated noise, and at practitioners assembling stochastic ensembles for ocean-atmosphere prediction. As ensemble ML weather models increasingly incorporate stochastic perturbations to represent unresolved processes, the mathematical machinery Holm reviews here has become directly relevant to operational forecasting.

items.title: Muon Space Closes $250M Series C at $1.5B Valuation — Eclipse Leads With Google, Salesforce Ventures, Galvanize Backing Earth-Observation Constellation Scale-Up
items.body_html: Satellite manufacturer Muon Space closed a $250 million Series C on August 20, 2026, lifting the San Jose, California company to a $1.5 billion post-money valuation and taking cumulative equity funding past $386 million. The round was led by Eclipse with participation from Google, Salesforce Ventures, Galvanize, Wellington Management, I Squared Capital, and Woven Capital, alongside existing backers Radical Ventures, Congruent Ventures, Costanoa Ventures, Activate, ACME, ArcTern, and Overlap. Muon plans to expand its San Jose plant to build up to 500 small satellites per year by 2027, targeting Earth-observation and remote-sensing constellations relevant to weather, climate, and defense customers. This is one of the largest Earth-observation-adjacent private rounds of Q3 2026 and directly relevant to buyers of weather-intelligence infrastructure — Muon's constellation ambitions target the same data-sparse regions where ML NWP models most benefit from new observation streams.

items.title: RockRose Risk Closes $12.5M Series A — Crosslink and Congruent Co-Lead Vertically Integrated Wildfire Insurance Platform Ahead of Peak Western Fire Season
items.body_html: San Francisco-based wildfire InsurTech RockRose Risk announced a $12.5 million Series A on August 19, 2026, co-led by Crosslink Capital and Congruent Ventures with participation from Nuveen. The broker/MGA-style firm offers property owners in California, Colorado, and Nevada discounted premiums in exchange for verified mitigation work, then intends to acquire tree-trimming and roofing companies so it can underwrite, inspect, and remediate wildfire risk in a single vertically integrated workflow. Proceeds will fund engineering and operations hiring plus expansion of the company's AI risk-scoring stack. Insurance Journal also covered the raise. The deal sits squarely in the wildfire catastrophe-risk analytics thesis — a category insurers have re-underwritten aggressively after 2020–2025 Western US loss experience — and lands ahead of the peak Western fire season with the CAMS Arctic-Circle and BC wildfire pictures reinforcing structural fire-risk repricing.

items.title: osapiens Acquires Nasdaq's Metrio ESG / Carbon-Accounting Platform — Terms Undisclosed; Deal Consolidates Sustainability-Reporting Software as Nasdaq Exits Category
items.body_html: German sustainability-software company osapiens announced on August 19, 2026 that it had acquired Nasdaq's Metrio sustainability-reporting and carbon-accounting platform; financial terms were not disclosed. Metrio covers CDP, GRI, IFRS S2, SASB, and California SB 253 / SB 261 disclosure frameworks, and the acquired customer book folds into the osapiens HUB alongside the company's supply-chain and compliance products. The deal follows osapiens' $100 million Series C earlier in 2026 co-led by BlackRock and Temasek's Decarbonization Partners, and is explicitly framed as an accelerator for U.S. expansion. A notable consolidation moment in the ESG / climate-reporting software category — Nasdaq is exiting a category it originally entered by acquiring Metrio in 2022, suggesting incumbents are ceding the disclosure-software layer to specialized European players as the CSRD, IFRS S2, and California SB 253 reporting cycle bites.

items.title: Cube Green Energy Names Felix Grolman Executive Chair — Former VSB Group CEO Joins I Squared-Backed European Renewables Developer
items.body_html: Renewables and battery-storage platform Cube Green Energy appointed Dr. Felix Grolman as executive chair on August 19, 2026. Grolman brings more than 15 years of leadership in European renewables and energy infrastructure, most recently as CEO of VSB Group, a major European renewable-energy project developer. The appointment signals that Cube's I Squared Capital-backed platform is pushing further into European origination and development ahead of expected offshore-wind and BESS auction cycles across Germany, Poland, and the Nordics. A notable executive move on the developer side of the renewables market as investors reposition around the post-2025 European tender pipeline — including Denmark's redesigned offshore-wind framework and Germany's Renewable Energy Directive III implementation.
